title: Ada and the Deadline
premise: Theo Iversen, a private security contractor who has spent fifteen years erasing themselves from every database, is guarding a client whose chartered flight vanishes from all records mid-air—yet the plane lands, and the client steps out as if nothing happened. Digging into the anomaly, Theo uncovers a data-scrubbing operation run by their own agency, one that rewrites the pasts of people deemed inconvenient. The trail leads to Ada, a teenage girl the agency erased years ago and Theo secretly sheltered—the one loose thread in an otherwise perfect system of forgetting. To save Ada, Theo must trade the flight's black-box evidence, the only proof the agency ever existed, in a final exchange where loyalty to found family finally outweighs the truth they've spent a career protecting.
about_author: Juniper Whitlock is a former aviation logistics analyst who left the industry after a project she still won't name. She writes thrillers about paper trails, quiet betrayals, and the people who fall through them.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A routine protection detail for a nervous tech executive establishes Theo's world: burner phones, cash routes, a life scrubbed so clean even Theo struggles to remember their own birthday. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness—competence as armor—until the executive mentions a charter flight that 'doesn't officially exist.'

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Mid-flight, every record of the plane evaporates: radar archives, booking manifests, even the pilot's license history. Yet it lands on schedule. Theo watches the client disembark smiling, and feels fifteen years of professional certainty crack. The beat is cold dread dressed as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Photographs
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Ada, sixteen, living under a false name in a coastal town—unaware her entire childhood was fabricated by someone who pays her rent anonymously. She finds a photograph of herself at age four in a house she's never seen. The beat is vertigo: the floor of identity giving way.

chapters.title: Clean Rooms
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Following the vanished flight leads to Meridian Group, the agency that employs Theo—and discovers its 'compliance division' doesn't just protect clients, it deletes people. Theo recognizes the deletion protocol: they helped write it. The beat is complicity turning to nausea.

chapters.title: Loose Threads
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Someone comes asking questions in her town; her anonymous benefactor goes silent mid-payment. She runs—not toward safety but toward the address on the back of the photograph. The beat is fear sharpening into resolve: if her past is a lie, she'll hunt the truth herself.

chapters.title: Intersection
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Theo traces the flight's passenger list to Ada's erased identity and realizes the agency has flagged her for final deletion. Before Theo can reach her, Ada walks into Theo's safehouse asking about the photograph. The beat is shock melting into fierce, terrified recognition.

chapters.title: What We Buried
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, flashback-laced. Theo confesses: fifteen years ago they smuggled a witness's daughter out of a cleanup operation and built her a new life—their single act of disobedience, hidden inside a career of erasure. Ada's anger and gratitude collide. The beat is raw honesty between two people made of aliases.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Meridian offers a trade: Ada's file stays buried if Theo hands over the black-box data proving Flight 4471 carried a whistleblower who never landed alive. Theo has seventy-two hours. The beat is the theme crystallized—loyalty versus truth, priced in blood.

chapters.title: Terminal Velocity
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. Theo stages a double-cross at a decommissioned airfield, broadcasting the flight data publicly while Ada triggers the deletion of Meridian's own archive—the machine eating itself. Gunfire, betrayal by Theo's oldest colleague, and a desperate runway escape. The beat is sacrifice without guarantee.

chapters.title: Unwritten
chapters.summary: Resolution, Ada's POV closing into shared narration. Meridian collapses quietly; the truth is out but half-buried, an imperfect victory. Theo, finally visible in the world, chooses a real name and lets Ada choose hers. They are not family by blood or law—just by decision. The beat is hard-won peace: memory kept, truth traded, loyalty honored.
